A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GTA-CLIP work. All 19 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material, support reliable comparison despite reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original zero-shot, few-shot, and seen-class experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and attribute visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and analyses in the main text and appendices, alongside revised computational-cost reporting.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same attribute-generation, transduction, and encoder-adaptation steps. The prompts, objectives, internal transduction call, and pseudo-label selection procedure remain substantively unchanged; revised generation hyperparameters concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 datasets under zero-shot and few-shot classification, with the same five-dataset seen/unseen-class evaluation. Appendix coverage is retained. CUB200/CUB and Caltech101/Caltech wording changes do not represent different datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix comparisons. In Table 3, CLIP-A-self becomes VDT, retaining citation [24], the same scores, and the same exclusion of its incompatible CUB setting.

E3.justification: Section 4 changes the maximum generation length from 1000 to 500 tokens. v2 Section 5.6 reports lowering alpha to 0.05 for ImageNet, whereas v1 specifies 0.1 across datasets. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish rerunning the unchanged accuracy tables. Other evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: The component and LLM-choice ablations, internal-transduction removal experiment, k/T/alpha sensitivity sweeps, and class-confusion analysis retain their evidence. All five detailed attribute case studies remain in the appendix, although Figure 2 displays fewer examples in the main text.

E5.justification: Both versions state that results are averaged over three runs. No repeated-run counts, seed disclosures, uncertainty estimates, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tabulated accuracies and confusion counts remain unchanged. Reported CUB runtime changes from roughly one hour to 12–20 minutes, with additional LLM timing, monetary-cost, and class-pair workload figures. These are revised resource results under changed reported settings, not demonstrated same-setting accuracy improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, Gaussian assumptions, assignment definitions, and optimization reasoning are retained. The attribute-count index cleanup and equation reflow do not introduce substantive mathematical changes; no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The three-stage contribution remains, but the abstract raises claimed average gains from 8.6%/3.7% to 9.5%/4.0% while retaining the three-encoder scope. Table 1 is unchanged: the latter figures describe ViT-B/16, not the cross-encoder average. The introduction also foregrounds the 12–20-minute computational-cost claim.

C2.justification: Section 6 removes the warning about benchmark-dependent LLM quality and possible degradation from pretraining mismatch. It instead says hallucinated attributes were not a significant issue on the studied datasets, citing AdaptCLIPZS. v2 also explicitly identifies streaming as incompatible with whole-test-set access and develops the cost-versus-manual-labeling argument.

D1.justification: Code changes from a promised release to a reported release at the same repository. v2 identifies Llama-3.1-8b and provides more detailed generation workloads, timing, API cost, and configuration information. The core optimizer and fine-tuning specifications remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 67 works remain cited. v2 narrows the blanket statement that no prior work demonstrated unlabeled-target-domain fine-tuning to a comparison with the reviewed approaches, foregrounds complementary integration, and more explicitly positions its attribute-based KL term relative to TransCLIP.

P1.justification: The Introduction and Related Work undergo extensive paragraph rewriting and reorganization of the contribution narrative. Resource requirements become a dedicated Computational Cost subsection; analysis headings, results prose, limitations, and acknowledgments are revised. This constitutes substantial language and narrative revision despite the stable technical framework.

P2.justification: Tables 1–3 receive angled headers and more compact formatting. Figure 2 changes from five examples spanning both columns to two examples in one column; all five detailed appendix plots remain. Captions and float placement change, while the underlying retained plots and table structures remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: v2 improves practical cost documentation, reports code availability, and clarifies presentation. However, its abstract replaces the supported cross-encoder gains with the stronger ViT-B/16 figures, while Table 1 and the introduction retain the original averages. The ImageNet alpha exception also conflicts with the retained statement that settings are fixed across datasets, and LLM limitations are softened without new validation. These documentation benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
